translated.evidence: We use the crowd-sourced English data that was professionally translated to 14 other languages for evaluation.

native_annotators.evidence: English data was crowd-sourced, then professionally translated. Annotators created English data; translators produced other languages.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Data is translated from English MultiNLI. No evidence of cultural adaptation for target languages.

XNLI.annotation_quality_notes: Professional translations of crowd-sourced English data from MultiNLI.

translated.evidence: The XCOPA authors translated and re-annotated the validation and test sets of the English COPA dataset into 11 languages.

native_annotators.evidence: XCOPA was translated and re-annotated, but the paper does not specify whether translators were native speakers of each target language.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Data is translated from English COPA. Causal reasoning scenarios are English-originated.

XCOPA.annotation_quality_notes: Translated and re-annotated from English COPA. Human performance estimated from annotator label disagreement.

translated.evidence: Test sets are independently annotated treebanks from the Universal Dependencies project.

native_annotators.evidence: Universal Dependencies treebanks are typically annotated by linguists and native speakers of each language.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Text sources vary per treebank; some use Wikipedia, others use varied native text. POS tagging is a structural task with less cultural dependency.

UD-POS.annotation_quality_notes: Independently annotated per-language treebanks from Universal Dependencies v2.7.

translated.evidence: Proper noun spans in Wikipedia text have been automatically annotated; test sets are independently annotated per language.

native_annotators.evidence: Annotations were automatic, not performed by human annotators.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Wikipedia text is in each target language, but annotation is automatic. Named entities may reflect local or global topics depending on Wikipedia content.

WikiANN-NER.annotation_quality_notes: Automatically annotated from Wikipedia. Silver-standard labels. Uses balanced splits from Rahimi et al. (2019).

translated.evidence: A subset of the English SQuAD v1.1 dev set was professionally translated into ten other languages for XQuAD.

native_annotators.evidence: Original questions and contexts are from English SQuAD, professionally translated. Original annotations were crowdsourced in English.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Content is translated from English Wikipedia-based SQuAD. Topics reflect English Wikipedia.

XQuAD.annotation_quality_notes: Professional translations of English SQuAD v1.1 subset.

translated.evidence: The evaluation data in seven languages was automatically mined from Wikipedia, annotations were crowd-sourced, and answer spans aligned. Table 2 lists test sets as 'translations'.

native_annotators.evidence: Annotations were crowd-sourced (not specified as native speakers) and answer spans were aligned across languages.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Data is mined from Wikipedia with aligned answer spans across languages. Table 2 lists domain as Wikipedia.

MLQA.annotation_quality_notes: Automatically mined from Wikipedia with crowd-sourced annotations and aligned answer spans.

translated.evidence: Table 2 lists TyDiQA-GoldP test sets as 'ind. annot.' (independently annotated).

native_annotators.evidence: TyDiQA is a benchmark for information-seeking QA in typologically diverse languages. Questions were written by native speakers of each language (per Clark et al., 2020).

culturally_grounded.evidence: Questions are independently created by native speakers in each language, reflecting genuine information needs.

TyDiQA-GoldP.annotation_quality_notes: Independently annotated. Gold passage version simplifies original task. Questions created by native speakers.

translated.evidence: Table 2 lists Tatoeba test sets as 'translations'. Consists of English-aligned sentence pairs.

native_annotators.evidence: Tatoeba is a community-contributed dataset. Contributors may be native speakers or learners.

culturally_grounded.evidence: English-aligned sentence pairs. Content is aligned to English source sentences.

Tatoeba.annotation_quality_notes: Community-contributed translations. Up to 1,000 English-aligned sentence pairs per language.

translated.evidence: Mewsli-X is automatically extracted from WikiNews articles in each language, with mentions linking to WikiData entities. Test sets are independently annotated (Table 2).

native_annotators.evidence: Data is automatically extracted from WikiNews hyperlinks, not human-annotated.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Mentions come from native-language WikiNews articles, so topics reflect news interests of each language community. However, entity descriptions span all 50 languages.

Mewsli-X.annotation_quality_notes: Automatically extracted from WikiNews. New dataset created for XTREME-R. 15K test mentions covering 9,647 distinct entities. Candidate pool of 1M entities across 50 languages.

translated.evidence: LAReQA XQuAD-R is derived from XQuAD translations. Table 2 lists test sets as 'translations'.

native_annotators.evidence: Derived from XQuAD professional translations of English SQuAD data.

culturally_grounded.evidence: Content originates from English SQuAD/XQuAD translations. Topics reflect English Wikipedia.

LAReQA.annotation_quality_notes: Derived from XQuAD translations. 13,090 questions with 11 target answers each across 11 languages.
